This is going to be one big PR that is a sweeping change and that is fine

result.output:
1	# Reserved Data Name `latest` — Repo-Wide Sweep
2	
3	Status: **plan, not started.** Written 2026-10-13 for a fresh session. Nothing
4	in this plan has been applied except the single `aws/dns-observation` fix noted
5	under "Already done".
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Current swamp rejects the data name `latest` at method run time:
10	
11	```
12	Error: Data name 'latest' is reserved for internal use in model
13	'@webframp/aws/dns-observation'. Use a different name.
14	```
15	
16	Observed on swamp `20261011.212318.0` running `@webframp/aws/dns-observation`
17	2026.09.24.1 `list_zones`. Many extensions in this repo pass `"latest"` as the
18	second argument of `context.writeResource(spec, "latest", data)`. Those methods
19	fail at run time on current swamp.
20	
21	**Why CI never caught it.** Extension tests use `createModelTestContext`, whose
22	mock `writeResource` accepts any name. `check`, `lint`, `fmt:check`, `test`, and
23	`swamp extension quality` all pass. Only a real swamp run (or the swamp runtime
24	validation) rejects the name. Any fix must add a guard that does not depend on a
25	live run.
26	
27	**Prior art.** `anthropic/analytics` hit this in July 2026 (#189) and renamed its
28	instance `latest` → `recent`, with a test asserting
29	`written.some((r) => r.name === "latest") === false`
30	(`anthropic/analytics/extensions/models/anthropic/analytics.ts:663`). The
31	pattern is known; it was never swept repo-wide.
32	
33	## Already done (do not redo)
34	
35	- `aws/dns-observation` 2026.10.13.1 — `list_zones` writes `zone-scan`,
36	  `detect_orphans` writes `orphan-scan` (`list_records` already used
37	  `record-scan`). Branch `fix/dns-observation-reserved-latest`, worktree
38	  `~/src/webframp/swamp-ext-dns-latest`, **uncommitted and unpushed** when this
39	  plan was written. Check `git branch -a`/`gh pr list` for its state. Do not
40	  duplicate it; exclude `aws/dns-observation` from the sweep once it has merged.
41	
42	## Scope (measured 2026-10-13, tracked files on `main`)
43	
44	A scan of tracked `*.ts` files for `writeResource|writeFile|readResource|readFile`
45	calls with a literal `"latest"` argument found **39 directories**: 36
46	extensions and 3 code generators. **Re-run the scan first** (see Phase 0) — the
47	counts below are a starting point, not a contract, and the scan pattern can miss
48	indirect forms.
49	
50	### Code generators (fix these first; they own generated output)
51	
52	| Generator | Evidence |
53	| --- | --- |
54	| `scripts/cloudflare-codegen` | `lib/method_classifier.ts:970` emits `writeResource("${resourceName}", "latest", ...)`; `:709` sets the action-instance constant to `"latest"` |
55	| `scripts/falai-codegen` | `lib/method_classifier.ts:1003` same emit; `:661` constant |
56	| `scripts/snyk-codegen` | `lib/method_classifier.ts:798` same emit; `:624` constant; `lib/test_generator.ts:455-458` expects `"latest"` |
57	| `scripts/datadog-codegen` | `lib/method_classifier.ts:626` constant; `lib/test_generator.ts:320` expects `"latest"` |
58	| `scripts/griptape-codegen` | `lib/method_classifier.ts:728,896` constant; `lib/test_generator.ts:503,509` fall back to `"latest"` |
59	
60	The first three emit the literal in a `writeResource` call. Datadog and Griptape
61	use the `'"latest"'` constant for the instance name, so their generated output may
62	use a variable instead of a literal and be invisible to the literal scan. Read
63	each generator, do not trust the grep.
64	
65	### Generated extensions (regenerate, never hand-edit)
66	
67	`CLAUDE.md` forbids hand-editing generated model files: "regenerate, then
68	validate both the generator and the affected extension." Each generator also
69	overwrites `README.md` and may refuse to overwrite `RELEASE_NOTES.md` without an
70	accurate note (`--notes` / `--notes-file`). See "Operational Workspace and Code
71	Generation" in `CLAUDE.md`.
72	
73	- `cloudflare/*` (21): access, api-shield, d1, email-routing, gateway, images,
74	  kv, load-balancing, magic-transit, pages, queues, r2, registrar, rulesets,
75	  spectrum, ssl-certificates, stream, vectorize, waiting-room, workers-ai
76	  (95 call sites), workers-scripts
77	- `falai/*` (5): account, assets, models, serverless, storage
78	- `snyk/*` (5): assets, groups, self, settings, slack
79	- `datadog/synthetics` (1)
80	
81	Confirm per directory that it is generator-owned before regenerating (some files
82	may have been hand-patched since generation).
83	
84	### Hand-written extensions (edit directly)
85	
86	- `aws/drift-state` — reads/writes a stored result named `latest`; log messages
87	  also say `'latest'` (`Failed to read stored drift result 'latest'`)
88	- `aws/config-compliance`
89	- `swamp-adoption`
90	- `aws/dns-observation` — covered by the existing branch, see above
91	
92	Re-check each: the scan found them via `readResource("latest")` /
93	`writeResource(..., "latest")` and the direct count was 0 for some because the
94	name goes through a variable.
95	
96	### Tests that assert `"latest"`
97	
98	10 test files assert the old name (for example
99	`snyk/groups/.../groups_test.ts`, `snyk/settings/.../settings_test.ts`,
100	`datadog/synthetics/.../synthetics_test.ts:732`). Generated tests come from each
101	generator's `test_generator.ts`; fix the generator, not the test.
102	
103	### Out of scope
104	
105	- The `.worktrees/` copies and `.claude/worktrees/` — local, untracked.
106	- `swamp.club` registry-side behavior. This plan fixes the repo.
107	- `~/src/disciplines/devsecops` local extensions: scanned, no hits.
108	
109	## Unknowns to resolve before changing code
110	
111	Do these in **Phase 0** and write the answers into this file.
112	
113	1. **Which call forms does swamp reject?** Confirm with a minimal local extension
114	   on the current swamp: `writeResource(spec, "latest", ...)`, a spec *named*
115	   `latest`, `writeFile`, and `readResource("latest")`. The error text says
116	   "Data name"; `readResource` of a name that can no longer be written is only a
117	   read problem if old data exists.
118	2. **Which swamp version introduced the check?** The Anthropic comment is from
119	   July, so the rule may be older than the failure, or enforcement may have
120	   tightened. This decides how urgent the older extensions are and whether any
121	   consumer is running a swamp that still accepts `latest`.
122	3. **Do already-published versions keep working for existing users?** Probably
123	   not on current swamp, which makes this a fix, not a feature. Say so in the
124	   release notes.
125	
126	## Naming decision
127	
128	The generators already distinguish instance kinds: `list` uses `"main"`, `action`
129	uses `"latest"`, and `get`/`update` key on a path id when one exists. Only the
130	`"latest"` constant and the writeResource emits need to change.
131	
132	**Recommendation: `"current"`** for the singleton instance everywhere (a stable,
133	descriptive name that does not collide with swamp's reserved word, and reads well
134	in `data.latest("<model>", "current")`). Alternatives used in this repo:
135	`recent` (Anthropic analytics), `<thing>-scan` (dns-observation). Decide once,
136	record it here, and use the same name in all generators so consumers learn one
137	rule.
138	
139	Rules for whatever name is chosen:
140	
141	- Deterministic. No timestamps (`CLAUDE.md`: "Deterministic resource instance
142	  names").
143	- Must not collide with another spec's instance of the same model: data names are
144	  per model, not per spec. `dns-observation` and `cfn-diagnostics` both hit this;
145	  see "Instance names must be collision-resistant" in `CLAUDE.md`.
146	
147	## Plan
148	
149	### Phase 0 — Reproduce and measure (no code changes)
150	
151	1. Create a worktree off `origin/main` (repo convention: `../swamp-ext-<topic>`,
152	   branch `fix/reserved-data-name-latest-...`).
153	2. Reproduce the error with a minimal extension; answer the three unknowns.
154	3. Re-run a broad scan and record exact lists in this file:
155	
156	   ```bash
157	   # literal call sites, including multi-line calls
158	   git ls-files '*.ts' | xargs grep -lzP \
159	     '(writeResource|writeFile|readResource|readFile)\(\s*(?:"[^"]*"|\w+|`[^`]*`),\s*"latest"|(readResource|getContent)\(\s*"latest"'
160	   # indirect forms: constants and ternaries that yield "latest"
161	   git ls-files '*.ts' | xargs grep -nE "['\"\`]latest['\"\`]" | grep -v _test.ts
162	   ```
163	
164	   Exclude `.worktrees/` and `.claude/worktrees/`.
165	4. Find consumers of the old names: README query examples, workflow YAML,
166	   reports, and any CEL such as `data.latest("<model>", "latest")`. Grep
167	   `*.md`, `*.yaml`, and report sources.
168	
169	### Phase 1 — Add a guard so this cannot recur
170	
171	Without this the sweep regresses the next time a generator or a new extension
172	copies the pattern. Choose one, then record the choice:
173	
174	- **Preferred:** a repo-level check in `scripts/ci-discover` or a new small
175	  script run by CI that fails when a tracked non-test `*.ts` file passes a
176	  literal `"latest"` as a data name. Reserved names should come from one list so
177	  other reserved words can be added.
178	- **Alternative:** a shared test helper in each generator that asserts no
179	  generated source contains the pattern, plus a conformance assertion in the
180	  generated tests (`assertEquals(written.some((r) => r.name === "latest"), false)`,
181	  as in the Anthropic fix).
182	
183	Whichever is chosen must run under the existing `deno task test` permissions
184	(`--allow-env --allow-net --allow-sys`), which have no file read access. A
185	static source-reading test in an extension failed for exactly this reason during
186	the dns-observation fix; put file-reading checks in a script with explicit
187	permissions instead.
188	
189	### Phase 2 — Fix the generators (one PR per generator)
190	
191	For each of `cloudflare`, `falai`, `snyk`, `datadog`, `griptape`:
192	
193	1. Change the emitted instance name and the action constant; update
194	   `test_generator.ts` to expect the new name.
195	2. Run the generator's own tasks: `deno task check`, `lint`, `fmt:check`,
196	   `test`.
197	3. Add a generator test that a generated model never writes the reserved name.
198	
199	### Phase 3 — Regenerate generated extensions (one PR per generator family)
200	
201	Per `CLAUDE.md`: start on a branch, run from `scripts/<name>-codegen`, scope
202	regeneration (`deno task generate -- --service <name>`), and pass
203	`--notes`/`--notes-file` with an accurate user-facing note; never an
204	initial-release placeholder.
205	
206	For every regenerated extension the usual coupling applies (`CLAUDE.md`, "A
207	version bump is coupled to three other things"): bump `manifest.yaml`, append an
208	identity entry to `upgrades:` whose `toVersion` equals the new version, update any
209	exact-literal `assertEquals(model.version, ...)`, and write `RELEASE_NOTES.md`.
210	
211	Then validate **each** affected extension, not only the generator:
212	
213	```bash
214	cd <extension>
215	deno task check && deno task lint && deno task fmt:check && deno task test
216	swamp extension quality manifest.yaml   # must be passed / 100%
217	```
218	
219	Inspect any `deno.lock` diff (`CLAUDE.md`: normal resolution refresh is
220	committed).
221	
222	### Phase 4 — Fix hand-written extensions (one PR, or one per extension)
223	
224	`aws/drift-state`, `aws/config-compliance`, `swamp-adoption`. Same coupling and
225	gates as above. For `aws/drift-state`, also update the log messages that quote
226	`'latest'`.
227	
228	### Phase 5 — Verify against a real swamp run
229	
230	Mock-context tests cannot prove the fix. For at least one extension per family
231	(one Cloudflare, one FAL AI, one Snyk, one Datadog if affected, `aws/drift-state`),
232	run a real method with a throwaway model and confirm the data is written under
233	the new name and `swamp data query 'model("<m>") && name == "current"'` returns
234	it. Read-only methods against a real account are fine; use the user's
235	`ReadOnlyPlus` AWS profiles for AWS ones. Do not run mutating methods to test.
236	
237	## Breaking-change handling
238	
239	Renaming a data name changes how consumers address stored data. State this in
240	every `RELEASE_NOTES.md`:
241	
242	**Changed:** stored data is now written as `<new-name>` instead of `latest`.
243	Anything that read `data.latest("<model>", "latest")`, or queried
244	`name == "latest"`, must use the new name. Data written under the old name cannot
245	be written again on current swamp and is not migrated.
246	
247	Follow `CLAUDE.md`: "Schema changes must be additive" governs attribute schemas
248	(unchanged here); the name change is the user-visible break, so give it an
249	explicit **Upgrade note**. The `upgrades:` entry is an identity migration
250	(`(old) => old`) because attributes do not change.
251	
252	## PR structure
253	
254	Small, independent PRs; every PR bumps the manifest in its first commit.
255	
256	1. Phase 0/1: guard (script or helper) plus this plan updated with findings.
257	2. One PR per generator (Phase 2), then one regeneration PR per generator
258	   family (Phase 3). Keep them separate: a generator change reviewed together
259	   with 20+ regenerated extensions is unreviewable.
260	3. Hand-written fixes (Phase 4).
261	
262	Follow `skills/pr-workflow.md`. Local adversarial review (`git diff
263	origin/main...HEAD`) before every push. Mirror every `ci.yml` job locally,
264	including `swamp extension quality`, before pushing. CI uses Deno 2.9.7
265	(`env.DENO_VERSION` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Tag @webframp on each PR;
266	only they can approve CI and issue `/lgtm`.
267	
268	## Risks
269	
270	- **Scale.** About 21 Cloudflare extensions plus 11 other generated ones means
271	  dozens of version bumps and publishes. Batch regenerations by family so a
272	  rollback reverts one family.
273	- **Silent consumer breakage.** Workflows, reports, or dashboards in other repos
274	  (for example `~/src/disciplines/devsecops`) may reference `"latest"`. The scan
275	  of the DevSecOps workspace found none in `extensions/`, but check its
276	  workflows, models, and reports before announcing.
277	- **Name collisions.** A new singleton name must not collide with another
278	  instance of the same model. Check each extension for existing `"current"`
279	  usage before regenerating.
280	- **Partial detection.** The literal scan misses constants and ternaries. Phase 0
281	  and Phase 1 exist to close that gap; do not skip them.
282	- **A reserved word beyond `latest`.** The error message does not list other
283	  reserved names. If Phase 0 finds more, extend the guard's list.
284	
285	## Definition of done
286	
287	- No tracked, non-test `*.ts` passes a reserved name as a data name; the guard
288	  from Phase 1 enforces it in CI.
289	- All five generators emit the chosen name and test for it.
290	- Every affected extension is regenerated or fixed, version-bumped, release-noted,
291	  and passes check/lint/fmt/test and `swamp extension quality` at 100%.
292	- At least one real swamp run per family confirmed the data lands under the new
293	  name.
294	- This file is updated with the Phase 0 answers and the final PR list.
295	
296	## Handoff checklist for the new session
297	
298	1. Read `CLAUDE.md` (the whole file, especially Versioning, Dependency Import
299	   Specifiers, Release Notes, and the codegen notes).
300	2. Load the `swamp` skill; run `swamp model search --json` per repo guidance.
301	3. Check the state of `fix/dns-observation-reserved-latest`.
302	4. Do Phase 0 before touching any generator.
303	5. Decide the new name with the user, record it above, then proceed.
304	
305	## Addendum: `aws/drift-state` findings and recommendations
306	
307	Added 2026-10-13 after the pre-push review of the `aws/dns-observation` fix
308	(PR #487). `aws/drift-state` (2026.09.25.1) is in the sweep's hand-written
309	group. Treat it as the **first** extension of Phase 4: it is small, has no
310	generator behind it, and it surfaced two problems the generic plan did not
311	anticipate.
312	
313	### What it does today
314	
315	All line numbers are in `aws/drift-state/extensions/models/aws/drift_state.ts`
316	at 2026.09.25.1; re-check them before editing.
317	
318	| Site | Line | Kind | Spec | Data name |
319	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
320	| `compute_drift` result | 986-988 | write | `driftResult` | `latest` |
321	| `get_drifted` read | 1171 | read | (expects `driftResult`) | `latest` |
322	| `get_drift_velocity` read | 1297 | read | (expects `driftResult`) | `latest` |
323	| `get_drift_velocity` write | 1312 | write | `velocity` | `latest` |
324	| `get_drift_velocity` write (final) | 1378-1380 | write | `velocity` | `latest` |
325	
326	Two log messages quote the name: `Failed to read stored drift result 'latest'`
327	(~1179) and `... 'latest' for velocity` (~1305). The test file keys its mock
328	`storedResources` by `latest` (~764, 822, 1013).
329	
330	Not affected: `baseline` is written under the source name, `timeline` under
331	`timeline-<hash>`, and `drifted` under `query`. Existing baselines and
332	timelines therefore survive the rename untouched.
333	
334	### Finding 1: two specs already share one data name
335	
336	Data names are per model, not per spec. `compute_drift` writes `driftResult` as
337	`latest` and `get_drift_velocity` writes `velocity` as `latest`. Both land on the
338	same data name, and both `get_drifted` and `get_drift_velocity` read `latest`
339	expecting a `driftResult`.
340	
341	Whether swamp versions the second write under the same name (so
342	`get_drifted` could read a `velocity` payload after `get_drift_velocity` ran) or
343	rejects the write is **unverified**. Phase 0 must settle it with a throwaway
344	model before anyone relies on either reading. Either way it is a latent bug
345	independent of the reserved word, and the fix removes it.
346	
347	This also corrects the plan's naming recommendation. **A single shared name such
348	as `current` is wrong for any model with more than one singleton spec**: a
349	second spec using `current` collides with the first, which is the same bug.
350	Recommend `<spec>-current` (for example `drift-result-current`,
351	`velocity-current`) wherever a model has more than one singleton spec, and add a
352	collision check to Phase 0: for each affected extension, list every data name
353	across all of its specs and confirm they are unique.
354	
355	### Recommendations
356	
357	1. **Rename to distinct, descriptive names.**
358	   - `driftResult` → `drift-result`
359	   - `velocity` → `drift-velocity`
360	   - Update all five sites, both log messages, and the mock keys in the tests.
361	   - Keep the reads and writes in lock-step: `get_drifted` and
362	     `get_drift_velocity` must read `drift-result`, the name `compute_drift`
363	     writes.
364	2. **No data migration.** `compute_drift` and `refresh` regenerate the result
365	   from upstream data on demand, and baselines and timelines keep their names.
366	   Say so in the release notes: after upgrading, run `compute_drift` (or
367	   `refresh`) once, because `get_drifted` and `get_drift_velocity` return empty
368	   results until it has written the new name. The existing README entry
369	   "`get_drifted` / `get_drift_velocity` return empty results" (~line 84) is the
370	   right place for this; extend it.
371	3. **Do not touch how upstream data is read.** `compute_drift` reads other
372	   models with `dataRepository.findBySpec(modelName, specName)` (~line 716)
373	   using the `SOURCES` map (`orphans`, `compliance`, `scan`, `discovery`,
374	   `read_state`, `graph`). That addresses upstream data by **spec**, so the
375	   `dns-observation` rename (PR #487) and a future `config-compliance` rename
376	   are invisible to it. Do not "fix" `SOURCES`.
377	4. **Version and release.** Bump `manifest.yaml` and `model.version`, append an
378	   identity `upgrades` entry (the last `toVersion` is `2026.09.25.1`), update any
379	   exact-literal version assertion, and write `RELEASE_NOTES.md` with an explicit
380	   **Changed** line: stored results are now `drift-result` / `drift-velocity`
381	   instead of `latest`; anything reading `data.latest("<model>", "latest")` must
382	   change. Follow the coupling rules in `CLAUDE.md`.
383	5. **Tests.**
384	   - Assert the written names for `compute_drift` and `get_drift_velocity`.
385	   - Assert that no two resources written in one run share a name (this catches
386	     the cross-spec collision, which the mock context does not).
387	   - Assert the readers look up the name the writer produces: seed
388	     `storedResources` with the new name and confirm `get_drifted` and
389	     `get_drift_velocity` find it.
390	6. **Check consumers before announcing.** Look for the `drift-state-refresh`
391	   workflow (the manifest refers to it) and any report or workflow that reads
392	   `drift-state` data by name, in this repo and in `~/src/disciplines/devsecops`.
393	   The scan so far found no consumer outside `aws/drift-state` in this repo.
394	7. **Verify against a real swamp run (Phase 5).** The extension reads other
395	   models' stored data, so a full run needs upstream models. A cheaper check
396	   still proves the names: run `compute_drift` with no upstream data. It reports
397	   every source as unavailable but still writes a `driftResult`. Confirm it lands
398	   under `drift-result`, then run `get_drifted` and `get_drift_velocity` and
399	   confirm they read it and write `drift-velocity`.
400	
401	### Suggested PR
402	
403	One PR, `fix(aws/drift-state): stop writing reserved data name 'latest'`, kept
404	separate from the generator work. Land it right after #487 merges so
405	`dns-observation` and `drift-state` stop failing together. Open items for the PR
406	description: the cross-spec collision (Finding 1), the "run `compute_drift` once
407	after upgrading" note, and the unverified swamp behaviour from Phase 0.
408	
409	### Sweep-wide lessons from this review
410	
411	- A rename is not finished until every **reader** is found. The `dns-observation`
412	  fix was safe because its consumer reads by spec; `drift-state` reads its own
413	  results by name. Grep for `readResource(` and `data.latest(` next to every
414	  `writeResource(` change.
415	- Add the "data names are unique per model across specs" check to the Phase 1
416	  guard, not just the reserved-word check.
417	- The mock `writeResource` hides both problems (reserved word and collision).
418	  Tests for every touched extension should assert written names explicitly.

# Swamp

## Core Concepts

- **Models** — typed resource definitions exposing methods (create, stop,
  destroy, sync).
- **Data** — versioned state snapshots produced by method runs; referenced via
  CEL expressions.
- **Workflows** — declarative DAGs chaining model methods with guard expressions
  for idempotent execution and assert steps for validation.
- **Vaults** — secret storage referenced by models at runtime.
- **Extensions** — TypeScript packages adding model types, vault backends,
  datastores, reports, and webhook handlers.
- **Grants** — authorization rules for swamp serve access control.
- **Serve** — exposes the repo over the network with TLS and authentication.

## Routing Table

Route to the right guide based on what the user needs.

| User intent                                                   | Guide                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Models — create, run, edit, delete, search types              | [references/model/guide.md](references/model/guide.md)                         |
| Workflows — create, run, validate, DAG, history               | [references/workflow/guide.md](references/workflow/guide.md)                   |
| Data — list, query, versions, GC, delete                      | [references/data/guide.md](references/data/guide.md)                           |
| Vaults — create, store/read secrets, expressions              | [references/vault/guide.md](references/vault/guide.md)                         |
| Reports — run, configure, view, filter                        | [references/report/guide.md](references/report/guide.md)                       |
| Repository — init, upgrade, datastores, sources               | [references/repo/guide.md](references/repo/guide.md)                           |
| Extensions — create models/vaults/datastores/reports/webhooks | [references/extension/guide.md](references/extension/guide.md)                 |
| Publishing — push extensions to registry, deprecate           | [references/extension-publish/guide.md](references/extension-publish/guide.md) |
| Issues — file bugs, features, security reports                | [references/issue/guide.md](references/issue/guide.md)                         |
| Run tracking — active runs, stale detection, diagnostics      | [references/model/guide.md](references/model/guide.md)                         |
| Architecture — which primitive to use, design trade-offs      | [references/architecture/guide.md](references/architecture/guide.md)           |
| Sharing — promote solo repo to team, datastore + vault setup  | [references/share/guide.md](references/share/guide.md)                         |
| Serve — auth, grants, access control, tokens, OAuth           | [references/serve/guide.md](references/serve/guide.md)                         |
| Troubleshooting — errors, health checks, diagnostics          | [references/troubleshooting/guide.md](references/troubleshooting/guide.md)     |

## Common Commands

```bash
# Models
swamp model create <type> <name>               # create a model definition
swamp model @<type> method run <method> <name> # run a method on a model
swamp model get <name> --json                  # inspect current model state
swamp model type search [query]                # find available model types
swamp model list                               # list all models in the repo

# Data
swamp data list <name>                         # list data versions for a model
swamp data query '<CEL predicate>'             # query data with CEL expressions
# read one item's latest content (`swamp data get` is deprecated)
swamp data query 'model("<model>") && name == "<data>"' --select content

# Workflows
swamp workflow create <name>                   # create a new workflow
swamp workflow validate <name>                 # validate DAG before running
swamp workflow run <name>                      # execute a workflow
swamp workflow run <name> --input key=value    # execute with inputs
swamp workflow resume <name>                   # resume a suspended workflow
swamp workflow resume <name> --run <id>        # retry a failed run's failed steps
swamp workflow resume <name> --from <step>     # re-enter failed run at step
swamp workflow history search --json           # search run history

# Run tracking
swamp run history                              # recent runs (last 24h)
swamp run history --active                     # what's running right now?
swamp run doctor                               # diagnose stale/orphaned runs
swamp run doctor --fix                         # auto-reap stale runs

# Vaults, Reports, Extensions
swamp vault create <type> <name>               # create a vault for secrets
swamp report run <name>                        # run a report
swamp extension init <name>                    # scaffold a new extension
```

## Workflow

1. **Route** — match intent to a guide in the routing table.
2. **Load** — read the guide; load its `reference.md` if needed, deeper
   `references/` only when the guide says to.
3. **Validate** — before running any workflow: `swamp workflow validate <name>`.
   Before destructive methods (delete, stop, destroy):
   `swamp model get <name> --json` to confirm the target exists and is in the
   expected state. Proceed only when validation passes.
4. **Verify args** — run `swamp help <subcommand>` (e.g.
   `swamp help model method run`) to confirm exact flags and arguments before
   executing. The output is structured JSON — the canonical CLI schema.
5. **Execute** — run the command.
6. **On failure** — load
   [references/troubleshooting/guide.md](references/troubleshooting/guide.md)
   and diagnose before retrying or changing definitions.

## Rules

1. **Use the routing table, not memory.** Don't answer from cached knowledge
   about swamp commands — always load the current guide.
2. **Consult the architecture guide for design decisions.** Before choosing
   between primitives (model vs. workflow vs. extension vs. report) or
   explaining a design trade-off, load
   [references/architecture/guide.md](references/architecture/guide.md) and cite
   the design doc you relied on.
3. **Use swamp commands, don't go around them.** Query data with
   `swamp data query`, not by grepping `.swamp/` files. Interact with resources
   through model methods, not raw CLI tools when a model type already wraps the
   API — check with `swamp model type search`. Composing with `--json` output
   (e.g. piping through `jq`) is fine — the anti-pattern is bypassing swamp
   entirely.
4. **Verify flags with `swamp help` before executing.** `swamp help <command>`
   outputs the full CLI schema as structured JSON — every subcommand, argument,
   and option. Always run it to confirm exact flags before executing a swamp
   command (workflow step 4). Do not guess flags from memory.

# Pre-Push Review Loop

Run a local adversarial review on uncommitted or unpushed changes. Iterate
until the review passes, then stop and ask the human for push confirmation.

## When to Use

After making changes and before pushing to a remote branch. Especially
critical for:
- Fixes to prior adversarial review findings (regression risk is high)
- Concurrent-access code (locks, sequences, distributed state)
- Any change touching error handling or fallback paths
- New code (>200 LOC) — fresh code has too much surface area for a single pass

## The Loop

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                     │
│  ┌──────────┐    ┌───────────┐    ┌──────────────┐ │
│  │  SHOW    │───►│   RUN     │───►│  EVALUATE    │ │
│  │  DIFF    │    │  GATES    │    │  VERDICT     │ │
│  └──────────┘    └───────────┘    └──────┬───────┘ │
│                        ▲                 │         │
│                        │           ┌─────┴─────┐   │
│                        │           │           │   │
│                        │         PASS        FAIL  │
│                        │           │           │   │
│                        │           ▼           ▼   │
│                        │     ┌──────────┐ ┌──────┐ │
│                        │     │  ASK TO  │ │ FIX  │ │
│                        │     │  PUSH    │ │      │ │
│                        │     └──────────┘ └──┬───┘ │
│                        │                     │     │
│                        └─────────────────────┘     │
│                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Phase 1: Show Diff

Collect the changes to review:

```bash
# Uncommitted changes against HEAD:
git diff HEAD

# Or unpushed commits against remote:
git diff origin/main...HEAD
```

Use whichever is appropriate. If there are uncommitted changes, review those.
If all changes are committed but unpushed, review the full branch diff.

## Phase 2: Run Quality Gates

Before sending to the reviewer, verify the code compiles and passes local
checks. This phase has two parts: standard gates and repo-specific gates.

### 2a. Standard Gates

Discover gates from the project's config files:

| Config file | Commands |
|-------------|----------|
| `deno.json` | `deno task check && deno task lint && deno task fmt:check && deno task test` |
| `package.json` | `npm run lint && npm run build && npm test` |
| `Cargo.toml` | `cargo check && cargo clippy && cargo test` |

If gates fail, fix them first. Do not send broken code to the reviewer.

### 2b. Repo-Specific CI Gates

Standard gates catch compile/lint/test failures. They do NOT catch structural
or convention failures that CI validates separately.

**Always check for repo-level guidance first.** Read steering files, skills,
CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, or contributing docs in the target repository. These
define what CI expects beyond standard compilation. Follow that guidance
exhaustively — run EVERY command listed, not a subset. Skipping a single
command from the checklist is the same as skipping Phase 2 entirely.

If no explicit guidance exists, fall back to these heuristics:

1. **Check CI workflow files** (`.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`).
   Identify validation steps beyond standard gates and run them locally.

2. **Compare directory structure against a peer.** In repos with many
   packages of the same kind, your new addition must match the structure
   of existing ones (marker files, metadata files, test file conventions).

3. **Run repo-specific validation commands locally.** If CI runs a
   validation command, run it yourself first.

**The principle:** if CI will run it, you run it first. "It compiled and
the tests passed" is necessary but not sufficient.

## Phase 3: Adversarial Review via Subagent

The subagent MUST have the same capability as a CI adversarial reviewer.
A diff blob with prose context is insufficient — the reviewer must read
the actual source files to trace execution paths, verify cross-function
consistency, and find protocol-level issues.

### Subagent Setup

Use a `general-task-execution` subagent. Provide:

1. **File paths to read** — tell the subagent which source files to read
   in full. The diff identifies *what* changed; the source files reveal
   *what interacts with* what changed. The subagent must read the complete
   implementation files, not just the diff.

2. **The diff** — for awareness of what's new vs existing code.

3. **Protocol and boundary context** — describe the external system's
   interface contract. For APIs: how input is parsed (line-delimited?
   shell-tokenized? JSON?). For CLI wrappers: how arguments are
   concatenated. For network protocols: framing, escaping, delimiters.
   The reviewer cannot find injection bugs without understanding the
   protocol boundary.

4. **Sibling consistency requirement** — if the code has multiple
   functions that do similar things (e.g., multiple command builders,
   multiple SSH invocations), explicitly instruct the reviewer to verify
   that ALL siblings apply the same validation/escaping/timeout patterns.
   Inconsistency between siblings is the #1 class of bug that single-pass
   reviews miss.

### Review Prompt Requirements

The subagent's review instructions MUST include these specific probes
(not just "assume broken"):

1. **Trace every interpolation site.** For each user-supplied value that
   ends up in a command string, network request, or file path: what
   characters can break the framing? Spaces, newlines, quotes, semicolons,
   pipes, backticks, dollar signs, null bytes — each has meaning in
   different contexts.

2. **Verify sibling consistency.** If function A validates input X, do
   ALL functions that accept the same class of input apply the same
   validation? List every sibling and confirm.

3. **Check timeout/resource bounds on every external call.** Every
   subprocess spawn, every network request, every fan-out: is there a
   hard deadline? What happens if it hangs? What happens if output is
   unbounded?

4. **Test with concrete breaking inputs.** For each finding, provide the
   exact input string that breaks it. "This could be a problem" is not a
   finding — "input X produces output Y which the server interprets as Z"
   is a finding.

5. **Verify the bootstrap/lifecycle path.** Can the code be invoked in
   the order the documentation describes? Are there circular dependencies
   between configuration and the methods that produce that configuration?

6. **Check truthiness vs nullability.** In JavaScript/TypeScript,
   `if (x)` skips `0`, `""`, `NaN`, `null`, `undefined`. For numeric
   parameters, `0` is often a valid value. For optional strings, `""`
   may be meaningful.

### Verdict Format

Require the subagent to produce:

```
### [CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW] <title>
**File:** <path>
**Line(s):** <range>
**Issue:** What is wrong
**Breaking input:** The exact value that triggers the bug
**Impact:** What breaks
**Fix:** How to fix it

## VERDICT: PASS or FAIL
```

FAIL if any CRITICAL or HIGH findings exist. PASS otherwise.

## Phase 4: Evaluate Verdict

| Verdict | Action |
|---------|--------|
| PASS (no HIGH+) | Proceed to Phase 5 |
| FAIL (any HIGH+) | Fix findings, return to Phase 2 |

### On FAIL

- Fix ALL findings (HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW). Do not defer.
- After fixing, re-run quality gates (Phase 2)
- Re-run the adversarial subagent (Phase 3) on the CURRENT source files
- The re-review MUST re-read the source files — do NOT just re-review
  the new diff. Fixes often introduce new inconsistencies.
- Do NOT push between iterations

### Minimum Iterations

- For new code (>200 LOC of implementation): run at minimum 2 review
  iterations even if the first passes. Fresh code has too much surface
  area for a single pass to catch everything.
- For fixes to existing code (<50 LOC): one passing iteration is
  sufficient.

### Iteration Cap

Maximum 5 review iterations. If still failing after 5:
- Summarize what was fixed
- List remaining findings
- Ask the human for guidance — do not push in a failing state

## Phase 5: Ask to Push

When the review passes:

1. Show a brief summary of what changed
2. State: "Local adversarial review passed. Ready to push?"
3. **Wait for explicit human confirmation**
4. Only push after the human says yes

## Rules

- NEVER push without human confirmation, even on PASS
- NEVER skip Phase 2 (quality gates) — broken code wastes review cycles
- NEVER send only a diff to the reviewer — the subagent must read the
  full source files. A diff is supplementary context, not the primary input.
- NEVER defer a finding. Fix ALL findings before the next iteration.
  Deferral is not your decision — only the human can choose to ship with
  a known issue. If you think something should be deferred, ask
  explicitly. Otherwise, fix it.
- If the same finding appears twice across iterations, try a fundamentally
  different approach rather than tweaking the same fix
- After fixing findings, the re-review must check that the fix didn't
  introduce inconsistency with sibling code. Fixing function A without
  applying the same fix to sibling functions B and C is the most common
  regression pattern.
- The subagent review has confirmation bias limitations (it reads with
  fresher eyes than you, but still runs on the same model). Expect CI to
  occasionally catch things the local loop misses — but "occasionally"
  means one finding, not six rounds of fixes. If CI finds more than one
  HIGH after your pre-push loop, the loop was run incorrectly.

Every extension is licensed under **Apache-2.0**, matching the repository root
`LICENSE`. There is exactly one canonical form:

- **License type:** Apache-2.0. No MIT, no other license. Each extension ships a

- **Copyright line:** exactly `Copyright 2026 Sean Escriva` (Apache style, no

  quality rubric earns the `has-license` point from a shipped license file at
  the tarball root, so every extension lists `LICENSE.md` under
  `additionalFiles:` (or the `paths.base: manifest` opt-in). Do **not** add a
  top-level `license:` field to `manifest.yaml` — it is redundant with the
  shipped file and creates drift.

- **Why the final gate is green:** the blocking check at `ci.yml:478-481` filters the same way, so it never sees the review. That is why every check is green while GitHub still says BLOCKED.
